title: Parameterise SQL; never interpolate or concatenate it

facts.note: Bun stack/runtime scope: the repository (or package containing the changed file) is a Bun project, established by a stack observer that detects a Bun lockfile or bunfig.toml at the project root, or a file importing bun:sqlite / using Bun.sql. Language alone cannot distinguish Bun from Node.js, so this fact is required; no current observer reports project-level stack membership for a changed file, hence needs_new_observer.
Code language of the changed file. Necessary but not sufficient: it must be combined with the Bun stack fact. Applies to source and test files alike; no file-kind restriction in the source.

Code-level observer: SQL text is passed to a bun:sqlite query/run/exec/prepare call, Bun.sql, or a postgres/mysql client method. Applies to any such call (new, edited or existing being worked on); this is a scope signal, not an exclusive gate. Facts are conjunctive: Bun stack AND JS/TS language AND a query-sink call carrying SQL text.

fires: In a Bun project, a bun:sqlite query/run/exec/prepare call receives an untagged template literal with a SQL keyword and a ${} interpolation.
In a Bun project, a bun:sqlite query/run/exec/prepare call receives a quoted SQL string followed by + concatenation.
In a Bun project, a postgres/mysql client method receives an untagged SQL template literal with ${} interpolation.
In a Bun project, a postgres/mysql client method receives a quoted SQL string concatenated with +.
In a Bun project, SQL text built by interpolation or concatenation is passed to Bun.sql as a plain string (not as a tagged template).
Any of the above shapes, in a Bun project, appears in a test file or in an existing call being touched.
doesNotFire: A tagged template such as sql`... ${id}` (Bun.sql binds each substitution).
A template literal containing no SQL keyword (not SQL).
Static SQL with no interpolation or concatenation.
A query sink called with a placeholder string plus bound parameters, e.g. .get(id).
A postgres/mysql client call in a JavaScript/TypeScript project that is not a Bun project (e.g. a Node.js-only project); this Bun realization does not scope it.

given: Bun-project code calls a query sink (bun:sqlite query/run/exec/prepare, Bun.sql, or a postgres/mysql client method)
when: SQL text is passed to that sink
then: Do not build that SQL by interpolating an untagged template literal or concatenating strings; use a tagged sql`` template or placeholders with bound parameters.
prefer: db.query("SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = ?").get(id)  // bound parameter
await sql`SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = ${id}`  // Bun.sql binds
avoid: db.query(`SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = ${id}`)  // untagged: value spliced
A quoted SQL string followed by + and a value.
Mistaking an untagged template for a tagged one; they look almost identical.
unless: Tagged templates (sql`...`) are parameterised by construction and never flagged.
Template literals with no SQL keyword are not SQL and are skipped.
Static SQL with no interpolation is not injectable.
why: A tagged template parameterises each substitution; an untagged template or concatenation yields a finished string before the sink sees it, so values become SQL.
evidence: bun_security_hygiene_detector reports no SECURITY-SQL-INJECTION-001 finding on the touched files (a finding is verification evidence, not a precondition for applying the rule).
Reviewer confirms every query-sink call touched passes either static SQL with no interpolation or concatenation, placeholders with bound parameters, or a tagged sql`` template.
verifier_detail: Query sinks: bun:sqlite query / run / exec / prepare, Bun.sql, and postgres/mysql client methods (term query_sink: a call that executes SQL).
Flag a query-sink call whose first argument is a template literal containing both a SQL keyword and a ${} interpolation, or a quoted SQL string followed by +.

Term tagged_template: sql`…` — a template invoking a function that PARAMETERISES each substitution; safe by construction and visually almost identical to the untagged form that is not. The load-bearing subtlety: tagged is safe, untagged is not. The detector therefore flags only the untagged shape.
Skip: tagged templates; template literals with no SQL keyword; static SQL with no interpolation.
Severity 4; disposition strict (as stated in source metadata).
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.
Implementation: validator, ref bun_security_hygiene_detector (realizes core alias SECURITY-SQL-INJECTION-001).
Stack-neutral obligation, RE-REALIZED for Bun: the python-pytest sibling walks a Python AST for execute / executemany / raw / execute_sql and its own manifest scopes it 'python stack only'.
The tagged-vs-untagged template distinction has no Python analogue at all, which is why the rule had to be re-realized rather than translated.

additions.text: Activation facts and fires/doesNotFire examples, including a Bun stack/runtime fact (Bun lockfile/bunfig.toml or bun:sqlite/Bun.sql usage; needs_new_observer), the JS/TS language fact, and the code-level observer for SQL text passed to a query sink; non-Bun (e.g. Node.js-only) postgres/mysql calls listed as doesNotFire.
